name: The Bog Baby

inspiration.oldScript: Monstrous birth: the mutant baby and the mother blamed for it.
inspiration.newLens: The wetland drained and paved for a mall. The baby is the land, and the Best ending lets the marsh come back.

logline: They drained the marsh and paved it for parking, but something down there was about to be born. It has been drinking food-court grease for five years. This week it hatches.
backstory: Behind Starlight Mall there was Tule Marsh: two hundred acres of cattails, herons and chorus frogs around a deep pool that steamed in winter like something breathing. It was fed by the same cold spring as the old quarry lake, and on sunny days you could see violet crystals glittering on the bottom, little cousins of the Heartstone. Kids caught tadpoles there for a hundred years. The founders called it a swamp. In 1981 the county approved the mall's new Lot C, and in one summer the bulldozers drained the marsh, sealed the spring into culverts and poured asphalt over the deepest pool, which became Lot C. A biology teacher chained herself to a bulldozer and was fired for it. But the marsh had been getting ready for something. Two hundred acres of life had been folding itself into the deep pool like an egg, waiting to hatch, and the asphalt sealed it in. For five years the only thing that has reached it is what runs down the food court drains: fryer grease from Corn Dog Castle and Wok This Way, fifty gallons a night. It has been drinking. It has been growing. This Halloween week the soft spot in Lot C is warm to the touch, shopping carts are sinking into the asphalt, herons circle the parking lot at dusk, and from somewhere underground comes the sound of a thousand frogs crying like a baby that wants its mother.

centralIssue.title: Paved over for convenience
centralIssue.summary: The Bog Baby is a wetland that was never allowed to be born: two hundred acres of life buried under a parking lot so nobody would have to walk far to the Orange Jubilee. It eats grease because grease is all that reaches it. It doesn't need killing. It needs its water back.

poster: A colossal toddler-shaped creature of black mud and glistening golden grease rising out of a cracked mall parking lot at night, cattails crowning its head, a violet crystal heart glowing in its chest, a neon mall sign tilting behind it, tiny teens with flashlights at its feet
portrait: Close portrait of a giant baby-like face made of dripping marsh mud and shining fry oil, dozens of small frog eyes blinking across its cheeks, reeds and lily pads tangled in its hair, a violet glow from deep inside its open, wailing mouth
endingPhoto: A colossal toddler-shaped creature of black mud and golden grease sitting in a cracked mall parking lot under sodium lights, cattails in its hair, gently lifting a station wagon like a toy with a violet crystal heart pulsing in its chest, teens ducking behind shopping carts and a toppled mall sign in the background
taunts: Where is the water? Where did the water go?

clues.title: The Thing from Tule Marsh
clues.hint: One of Zelda Fishbein's old movies was shot on location at a marsh that isn't on any map anymore. Rewind Video has a copy in the horror aisle.

encounter.title: The Thing from Tule Marsh (1958)
encounter.text: Third shelf down, between The Blob and Them!, a battered clamshell case: THE THING FROM TULE MARSH, starring a young Zelda Fishbein screaming at something with too many reeds. The box is damp. The tape smells like pond water. When you pick it up, frogs start singing somewhere in the store, and the floor drain at the end of the aisle burps.
encounter.art: A video rental store horror aisle under pink neon, a battered clamshell videotape case of a 1950s creature movie with a painted marsh monster and a screaming blonde on the front, a damp ring of pond water spreading under it on the shelf, a teenager holding the case at arm's length, a floor drain at the end of the aisle bubbling up green water, pink neon and cold fluorescent light, medium shot

choices.label: Ask Zelda what it was like shooting on location

success.text: Zelda lights up. "Tule Marsh! Two weeks of night shoots. Herons, frogs so loud we had to redo every line, a pond that steamed like a teakettle in the cold. The monster was a stuntman in a rubber suit. The marsh was the real star." Her face falls. "They paved it for the mall. I sat in my car and cried." She gives you a lobby card: the marsh in full color, alive.
success.alone: The counter is unattended, but tucked inside the clamshell is a lobby card with a note on the back in red ink: Tule Marsh! Two weeks of night shoots, herons, frogs so loud we redid every line, a pond that steamed like a teakettle. The marsh was the real star. They paved it for the mall, and I sat in my car and cried. On the front: the marsh in full color, alive.
success.art: An older glamorous woman behind a video store counter handing over a vintage lobby card showing a lush 1950s marsh with herons and a steaming pond

failure.text: Zelda's on the phone with a distributor. You play the tape on the store monitor. The rubber monster on screen turns its head and looks right at you, and the picture fills with brown water that drips out of the bottom of the TV onto your sneakers.
failure.alone: Nobody's at the counter, so you play the tape on the store monitor yourself. The rubber monster on screen turns its head and looks right at you, and the picture fills with brown water that drips out of the bottom of the TV onto your sneakers.
failure.art: A store monitor showing a 1950s rubber swamp monster staring out of the screen, muddy water trickling from the bottom of the television onto a teenager's sneakers

choices.label: Watch the whole movie frame by frame for clues

success.text: The monster is fake but the location is real. In the opening shot there's a sign: TULE MARSH WILDLIFE REFUGE, EST. 1902. In the night scenes, at the bottom of the deep pool, something glitters violet, a cluster of crystal the size of a bathtub. The same stone as the Heartstone, alive under the water. Whatever is under Lot C was born from the same spring.
success.art: A paused television image of a 1950s marsh at night with a violet crystal cluster glowing at the bottom of a pond, a wildlife refuge sign visible in the reeds

failure.text: You fall asleep during the second reel and dream you're underground, under something hot and black and heavy, while overhead, all day long, car doors slam and slam and slam.
failure.art: A dreamlike view from deep underground looking up through layers of mud at the undersides of parked cars, faint golden light seeping through cracks

clues.title: The 1981 sit-in
clues.hint: KGLM broadcast live from a protest at the marsh in 1981. The tape is in the station archive, and the water tower has a view of Lot C.

encounter.title: View from the Tower
encounter.text: From the catwalk of the KGLM water tower you can see all of Glimmer Falls: the Crystal Street cul-de-sac, the high school, and Starlight Mall, a pink neon island in a sea of asphalt. From up here, Lot C isn't flat. The faded parking lines bulge in a shape like a pond, and in the middle, under the sodium lights, the asphalt is slowly rising and falling. Down in the booth, Mix has pulled an old reel labeled MARSH SIT-IN, 6/14/81.
encounter.art: A view from a water tower catwalk at dusk over a small California town, a teenager gripping the rail in the foreground, below them a pink neon shopping mall surrounded by gray parking lots, one far lot bulging up gently in the round shape of a pond with its faded parking lines curving over the swell, orange sodium lights flicking on, a small radio station shack at the base of the tower, purple and orange sky, high wide shot

choices.label: Listen to the sit-in reel with Mix

success.text: Over chanting and a diesel engine, a woman shouts: Opal Fairweather, Glimmer Falls High biology, chained to a bulldozer. "This marsh filters your drinking water! There are species here nobody's even named! Something is nesting in the deep pool!" Then a deputy, the clank of bolt cutters, and the DJ: "Well, folks, progress is progress." Mix stops the tape. "They fired her for that," he says quietly.
success.art: A teen DJ and a teenager listening to an old reel-to-reel tape in a dim radio booth, a faded 1981 photo of a woman chained to a bulldozer pinned above the console

failure.text: The reel plays nothing but frogs, louder and louder, until the board feeds back in a shriek and the whole water tower hums like a struck bell. Every dog in Glimmer Falls starts howling at once.
failure.art: A radio booth with a console shrieking feedback and a reel-to-reel spinning wildly, the water tower outside vibrating, dogs howling in yards below

choices.label: Climb to the top of the tank and photograph the lot

success.text: From the very top you snap an instant photo of Lot C. As it develops, it shows what your eyes can't: the cracks in the asphalt trace the exact outline of the old pond, and curled in the middle, glowing faintly gold through the blacktop, is something enormous shaped like a tadpole, with a violet heart.
success.art: A developing instant photo held up against the night sky, showing a parking lot with a giant glowing tadpole shape curled beneath the asphalt, a violet light at its center

failure.text: The ladder rungs are slick with something greasy. Your foot slips and you hang by your hands for one long, long minute while every frog in the county sings below you. You make it down. Your hands smell like corn dogs for two days.
failure.art: A teenager dangling by both hands from a slick water tower ladder high above the town at night, one sneaker kicking at empty air

clues.title: The grease trap
clues.hint: The night janitor at Starlight Mall says the food court drains have started flowing the wrong way.

encounter.title: Below the Food Court
encounter.place: The service corridor under the Starlight Mall food court
encounter.text: Behind Corn Dog Castle a service door leads down to a corridor that smells like a deep fryer's nightmare. Hector Villalobos, the night janitor, stands over a grease trap the size of a hot tub with a plunger in one hand and a rosary in the other. "Every night it drinks fifty gallons of fry oil," he says. "And every night, something down there says thank you."
encounter.art: A grimy concrete service corridor under a mall food court, pipes along the ceiling, a middle-aged janitor in gray coveralls holding a plunger in one hand and a rosary in the other beside a steel grease trap lid the size of a hot tub, golden light glowing up through the seams of the lid, a teenager crouched beside him, a caged work light overhead, low medium shot

choices.label: Help Hector heave the lid open and look

success.text: The lid comes up with a slurp. Grease spirals down a drain that goes far deeper than plumbing should, and from below comes a chorus of frogs and a slow, huge heartbeat. Hector unrolls the 1981 blueprints: the mall's storm drains run straight into the old marsh's deepest pool. "Whatever was in that pond," he says, "we've been feeding it french fries for five years."
success.art: A janitor and a teenager peering into an open grease trap that spirals down into glowing golden depths, old blueprints unrolled on the concrete floor beside them

failure.text: The lid slips. A geyser of warm golden grease erupts and coats you from head to sneakers. From somewhere far below, something giggles like a delighted baby.
failure.art: A teenager drenched head to toe in a geyser of golden grease erupting from a grease trap, a janitor shielding his face, the corridor lights flickering

choices.label: Ask Lou what the arcade kids have seen in Lot C

success.text: Lou doesn't look up from Starbug Blitz. "Dead-wing kids dare each other to stand on the soft spot in Lot C. It's warm, man. Like a waterbed. Last week it swallowed a shopping cart, and in the morning there were cattails growing out of the hole." He fishes one out of his backpack. Its fluff glows faintly gold in the dark of the arcade.
success.art: An arcade champion at a glowing cabinet holding out a single cattail whose fluff glows gold, other kids crowded around the machines in neon light

failure.text: Lou is one wave from a high score and can't talk. You go look for yourself. The soft spot gives under your sneaker like a warm mouth, and you yank your foot free minus one shoe.
failure.art: A teenager pulling their foot out of soft bulging asphalt in an empty parking lot at night, a sneaker sinking into the blacktop, steam rising

signature.title: The Soft Spot
signature.text: Lot C is empty except for one sputtering sodium light and a lone shopping cart in a parking space. The asphalt under the cart is bulging up like bread dough. Bubbles of golden grease ooze from the cracks. The cart sinks to its handle with a satisfied gloop, and then the sound rises out of the ground: a thousand frogs crying at once, like a baby who wants its mother.
signature.art: An empty mall parking lot at eleven at night under one sputtering orange sodium light, a lone shopping cart sunk to its handle in asphalt that bulges up around it, golden grease oozing from the cracks, a teenager in a jacket standing at the edge of the pool of light, the dark mall building far behind, orange light and black shadow, wide shot at ground level

choices.label: Grab the cart before it goes under

success.text: You plant your feet and heave. The cart comes free with a sucking pop, draped in duckweed, and sitting in the child seat is a small, very offended green frog. The ground stops crying. For tonight, it's been given something back.
success.art: A teenager hauling a shopping cart out of soft asphalt, the cart draped in duckweed with a small green frog sitting in the child seat

failure.text: The cart goes under and takes your sleeve with it. Warm mud closes around your arm to the elbow, and something down there holds on, curious, before letting you go. You stagger off coated in grease and cattail fluff.
failure.art: A teenager pulled down to the elbow into bubbling asphalt beside a vanishing shopping cart handle, golden light glowing beneath the surface

choices.label: Sing back to it, low and soft, like a lullaby

success.text: You kneel on the warm asphalt and hum the only lullaby you know. The bulge settles. The frog-crying softens into a sleepy croak. Right beside your knee, one single green cattail pushes up through the blacktop and opens.
success.art: A teenager kneeling and singing softly on a cracked parking lot under a sodium light, a single cattail sprouting through the asphalt beside them

failure.text: Your voice cracks on the high note. The crying turns angry, and every car alarm in Starlight Mall's parking lots goes off at once, a wall of honking and whooping that follows you all the way home.
failure.art: A teenager running across a parking lot as every car alarm blares and headlights flash, the asphalt behind them heaving

signature.title: Feeding Time
signature.place: Starlight Mall food court, after closing
signature.text: After closing, the food court is dark except for the neon of Corn Dog Castle. Every fryer has turned itself on. Grease bubbles over the counters in slow golden waterfalls, slides across the tile and pours into a crack that is splitting the fountain in two. Something under the mall is gulping and growing. The floor heaves. A pretzel kiosk tilts and begins to slide toward the crack.
signature.art: A dark mall food court after closing lit by the neon of a corn dog stand, every deep fryer switched on and spilling golden grease over the counters in slow waterfalls, the grease sliding across the tile floor into a widening crack that splits a tiled fountain in two, a pretzel kiosk tilting toward the crack, a teenager vaulting a counter, gold and pink neon light, wide shot

choices.label: Vault the counters and kill every fryer

success.text: Wok This Way, click. Corn Dog Castle, click. Taco Tuesday's, Spud Palace, Orange Jubilee, click, click, click. The golden waterfalls slow to drips. The crack in the floor grumbles, hungry and sulky, and shrinks to a hairline.
success.art: A teenager vaulting over a food court counter and slapping off a fryer switch, the river of grease slowing behind them, neon signs glowing

failure.text: You hit a slick of grease and skate across the tile on your back like a hockey puck, straight into the fountain. The crack opens under you and you hang onto the fountain's rim while pennies rain down past your face into the dark.
failure.art: A teenager clinging to the rim of a split mall fountain over a dark glowing crack, coins tumbling past them into the depths

choices.label: Crank the fountain valve and give it clean water instead

success.text: You find the fountain valve behind a fake plant and crank it wide open. Clean water floods into the crack. The gulping turns into a long, contented sigh, and up through the floor comes the sound of frogs singing like the first warm night of spring.
success.art: Clean water gushing from a mall fountain into a glowing crack in the floor, a teenager turning a valve behind a potted plant, faint green light rising from below

failure.text: The valve snaps off in your hand. Water and grease mix into a brown flood, the pretzel kiosk slides into the crack, and a moment later the crack burps a single soggy pretzel back at you.
failure.art: A pretzel kiosk tipping into a flooded crack in a mall floor, a teenager holding a broken valve handle, a soggy pretzel flying through the air toward them

signature.title: Something on the Roof
signature.place: The top deck of the Starlight Mall parking garage, overlooking Lot C, midnight
signature.text: The top deck of the parking garage is where Glimmer Falls teens go to park and look at the lights, and tonight you are up here in Wade's van with the radio on. The song cuts out. "We interrupt this broadcast," says a shaky KGLM announcer, "to report something large moving under Lot C." Then, on the roof of the van: a wet slap. Another. A slow, sticky dragging sound, like a webbed hand feeling its way toward the windshield.
signature.art: A black 1970s custom van with an airbrushed wizard on the side parked alone on the top deck of a mall parking garage at midnight, orange sodium lights, a muddy webbed handprint smeared across the windshield, two teenagers inside lit green by the dashboard radio, an 18-year-old with a long feathered dirty-blond mullet and a patched denim vest at the wheel, the lights of the town below, medium wide shot from the front

choices.label: Hit the gas and peel out down the ramp

success.text: The van screeches down five levels of ramps in a spiral, tires squealing, and something slides off the roof on the third turn with an offended croak. At the bottom you find a long smear of mud and duckweed across the roof and three bewildered bullfrogs riding in the luggage rack.
success.art: A van screeching down a spiral parking garage ramp with headlights blazing, a long streak of mud across its roof, three bullfrogs clinging to the luggage rack

failure.text: The van coughs and stalls. The radio crackles back on by itself, and out of it comes the sound of a thousand frogs crying. Mud slides down the windshield in a thick brown curtain, and the wipers only spread it around until dawn.
failure.art: Thick brown mud sliding down a van windshield as the wipers smear it, a dashboard radio glowing, frightened teenagers inside in a dark parking garage

choices.label: Roll down the window and pour out your cooler of ice water

success.text: You lean out and tip the cooler over the side. Ice water splashes across the concrete. The dragging stops. A long, cool, rubbery tongue unrolls past your face, laps up every drop, and withdraws with a satisfied gulp. In the morning there is a ring of cattails growing out of a crack on the top deck.
success.art: A teenager leaning out of a van window tipping a cooler of ice water onto concrete, a long rubbery frog-like tongue lapping the splash, cattails sprouting from a crack nearby

failure.text: You grab the wrong cooler and pour out a liter of Bolt Cola. The creature drinks it, every drop, and goes absolutely berserk with sugar, bouncing the van on its springs like a carnival ride until the hubcaps fly off.
failure.art: A van bouncing wildly on its springs on a parking garage deck, hubcaps flying off, a spilled soda puddle fizzing on the concrete, muddy handprints all over the doors

choices.label: Tune the radio to static and croak along with it

success.text: You find the static between stations and croak into it, deep and long. Wade joins in. The thing on the roof goes quiet, then croaks back, then the whole parking lot below joins in, a chorus of frogs echoing off the concrete. It sounds, for one second, like a summer night at a pond that is not there anymore.
success.art: Teenagers in a van croaking into a glowing dashboard radio, the whole moonlit parking lot below dotted with small frogs looking up, a soft mist rising from cracks in the asphalt

failure.text: You croak something rude by accident. The roof caves in an inch. A muddy webbed hand slaps the window right by your face and leaves a print the size of a hubcap, and Wade spends the next week trying to scrub it off.
failure.art: A giant muddy webbed handprint pressed against a van side window at night, a startled teenager recoiling inside, the van roof dented, sodium lights glowing over a lonely parking garage deck

signature.title: The Baby Monitor
signature.place: The Lindqvist bathroom, next door, 2 a.m.
signature.text: Bea's walkie-talkie crackles you awake. "Get over here. The baby monitor is picking up something, and it isn't my cousin." Through the little speaker on the Lindqvists' dresser comes a wet gurgle, then a hiccup, then a long, lonely wail. Bea's baby cousin, here for the week, is asleep in his crib, perfectly quiet. The sound is coming from the bathtub, where the drain is bubbling up duckweed, tadpoles and a slow tide of warm brown water that smells like the fryers at Corn Dog Castle.
signature.art: A pastel pink 1980s bathroom at two in the morning, a bathtub filling with warm brown water bubbling up from the drain, duckweed and tadpoles swirling on the surface, an 11-year-old girl with white-blonde braids, huge round red glasses and a yellow rain slicker over pajamas holding a baby monitor toward the tub, a teenager in the doorway holding a walkie-talkie, a single vanity light, medium shot

choices.label: Run the cold tap full blast and give it clean water

success.text: You crank the cold tap and let it run. The brown tide clears to green, then to clean. On the monitor, the wail softens to a gurgle, then a slow, sleepy croak, like a baby finally getting its bottle. Bea scoops three tadpoles into a jar. "For science," she says, and she is crying a little.
success.art: A bathtub of clear green water with tadpoles and duckweed floating gently, cold water pouring from the tap, a kid genius in pajamas holding up a jar of tadpoles

failure.text: The cold tap shrieks and spits out grease instead of water. The tub overflows across the tile, and both of you slip and go down together in a puddle of tadpoles. Mrs. Lindqvist finds you there at dawn and asks no questions, which is somehow worse.
failure.art: Two kids sprawled on a flooded bathroom floor in a puddle of murky water and wriggling tadpoles, an overflowing bathtub, grease dripping from the faucet

choices.label: Grab the plunger and fight it back down the drain

success.text: Plunge, plunge, PLUNGE. Something down there pushes back like a toddler refusing bedtime, then gives up with a long, sulky burp. The water drains away. On the monitor, the wail turns into a hiccupping sob, and then silence, and you feel oddly like you just won an argument with a baby.
success.art: A teenager working a plunger furiously over a bathtub drain as murky water swirls down, a kid genius cheering from the toilet lid, steam fogging the mirror

failure.text: The plunger gets sucked in to the handle with a pop and stays there, quivering. Then the drain spits it back at you along with a geyser of warm mud that paints the ceiling. Bea, dripping, says only, "Well, that was a hypothesis."
failure.art: A geyser of mud erupting from a bathtub drain and splattering a pastel bathroom ceiling, a plunger flying through the air, two kids dripping with mud

choices.label: Record the crying for Dr. Haddad to hear

success.text: You hold the recorder to the drain for ten full minutes. In the morning, Dr. Haddad listens with his eyes closed, then slows the tape down. Under the wail are heron calls, rain on cattails, and the deep, slow pulse of a spring. "That's not one animal," he says. "That's a whole marsh."
success.art: A veterinarian in a garage clinic listening to a cassette recorder with his eyes closed, a teenager and a kid genius leaning in beside him, jars of tadpoles on the shelf

failure.text: The tape plays back nothing but you, screaming, at double speed. Somehow, while you were holding the recorder to the drain, a frog got into your pajama pants. You do not remember screaming, but the tape does.
failure.art: A teenager hopping around a bathroom shaking a frog out of their pajama leg, a cassette recorder spinning on the edge of the bathtub, a kid genius laughing

signature.title: Locked In After Closing
signature.place: Pet Palace in Starlight Mall, after closing, 1 a.m.
signature.text: You hid in the stockroom on a dare and now the gates are down and the mall is dark. In Pet Palace every animal is awake: the turtles, the goldfish, the green anoles and a tank of fire-bellied toads, all pressed against the glass facing the same direction, toward Lot C. The aquariums are overflowing. The floor drain in the middle of the store gurgles, and a hand made of mud rises out of it, small and soft and grabbing, like a baby reaching for a mobile. Down the dark concourse, the mall cop's flashlight swings your way.
signature.art: A dark mall pet store at one in the morning, glowing aquariums overflowing water onto the tile, turtles, goldfish, green lizards and spotted toads pressed against the glass all facing the same wall, a small soft mud hand rising out of a floor drain in the middle of the store with its fingers spread, a teenager crouched behind a shelf of pet food, a flashlight beam swinging in from the dark concourse outside the gate, blue aquarium glow, wide shot

choices.label: Carry the frogs and turtles out the service door to the storm channel

success.text: Bucket by bucket you carry them out the service door to the concrete storm channel behind the mall, where a trickle of spring water still runs. The toads leap in singing. The mud hand in the drain waves after you, slow and sleepy, and sinks away. In the morning Pet Palace has a sign up: SHIPMENT MISSING, and the storm channel is full of song.
success.art: A teenager pouring a bucket of frogs and turtles into a moonlit concrete storm channel behind a mall, a trickle of clear water glowing, toads leaping and singing

failure.text: Halfway out the service door the bucket tips, and a dozen toads go bounding off down the concourse. The mall cop finds you on your hands and knees under the Orange Jubilee counter, chasing one. You spend the rest of the night explaining yourself to his flashlight.
failure.art: A teenager on hands and knees under a mall snack counter grabbing at a hopping toad, a security guard's flashlight beam pinning them in the dark

choices.label: Slip across into the boutique and freeze among the mannequins

success.text: You strike a pose between two mannequins in acid-wash and hold it. The flashlight sweeps over you and moves on. Then the mud hand oozes across the concourse, pats each mannequin on the shoe, curious, and pats yours too. It moves on. You breathe for the first time in a minute.
success.art: A teenager frozen in a pose between mannequins in acid-wash denim in a dark mall boutique, a small curious mud hand patting their sneaker, a flashlight beam sweeping past

failure.text: Your nose itches. You sneeze. The flashlight snaps to you, and so does the mud hand, which wraps itself happily around your ankle and holds on like a toddler at the shoe store. It lets go at dawn and leaves you with one very muddy leg.
failure.art: A teenager posed among boutique mannequins in acid-wash denim caught mid-sneeze in a security flashlight beam, a small soft mud hand wrapped happily around their ankle, a dark mall concourse behind

choices.label: Run to the mall cop and make him look at the drain

success.text: Officer Duane does not believe you, until he does. He shines his light on the drain just as the little mud hand gives him a wave. He sits down hard on a bench, takes off his hat, and says, "My granddad used to catch frogs out there, before the lot." Then he radios maintenance to shut off the grease line for the night.
success.art: A heavyset mall security guard sitting stunned on a concourse bench with his hat in his hands, his flashlight lighting a small mud hand waving from a floor drain, a teenager beside him

failure.text: He thinks you are the prank. By the time he turns his light on the drain there is only a puddle and a single cattail. He walks you out to the curb, writes you a trespassing warning, and tells your mother all about it in the morning.
failure.art: A mall security guard escorting a sheepish teenager out the glass doors of a dark mall at night, a lone cattail rising from a puddle behind them

signature.title: It's Hatching
signature.text: Lot C has split open like an eggshell. In the crater, wreathed in steam and cattails, something the size of a city bus is uncurling: a giant baby made of black mud and golden grease, its skin dotted with blinking frog eyes, a crown of reeds on its head and a violet light pulsing in its chest like a geode. It opens its mouth, and the wail rattles every window in Glimmer Falls. Parked cars are sliding into the crater. So is the edge of the mall's dead wing.
signature.art: A mall parking lot split open at three in the morning, in the steaming crater a creature the size of a city bus uncurling, a giant baby made of black mud and shining golden grease, dozens of small frog eyes blinking across its skin, a crown of reeds and cattails on its head, a violet light pulsing in its chest, parked cars tipping over the edge of the crater, teenagers with flashlights at the rim, orange sodium light and violet glow, wide shot

choices.label: Get the onlookers and their cars back from the edge

success.text: You wave flashlights, yell until your voice gives out, and bang on windshields. A line of cars reverses up the lot in a long string of headlights and nobody goes in. The baby wails, but it doesn't reach for anyone. It's scared too.
success.art: Teenagers waving flashlights and directing a line of reversing cars away from a steaming crater, a giant mud baby wailing but holding still in the pit

failure.text: A station wagon slides in and the baby pulls it under like a bath toy. The owner, safe at the edge in a bathrobe, screams about his warranty. You end up in mud to the waist and it takes three people to pull you out.
failure.art: A station wagon sinking into a muddy crater clutched by a giant baby's hand, a man in a bathrobe shouting at the edge, a teenager stuck to the waist in mud

choices.label: Climb down into the crater and touch its glowing chest

success.text: You slide down the mud and press your palm to the violet light. Suddenly you feel the marsh: herons lifting off at dawn, a summer pond full of tadpoles, the first frog of spring, and then the roar of the bulldozers and the heavy, hot dark. It stops wailing. A thousand frog eyes turn to look at you. "Mmmmama?" it croaks.
success.art: A small teenager in a muddy crater pressing a hand to the glowing violet heart of a giant mud baby, the creature gazing down at them with a thousand frog eyes, sudden calm

failure.text: The mud takes you to the knees, warm and pulling. It doesn't mean to hurt you. It's hugging. Your crew hauls you out by the armpits and you leave both your shoes behind as an offering.
failure.art: Friends hauling a mud-caked teenager out of a crater by the armpits, a giant mud baby's hand reaching after them gently, two sneakers sinking

signature.title: Something Drank the Milk
signature.text: At four in the morning a crash and a yelp bring you to the window. The Glimmer Dairy milk truck is stopped crooked in the middle of Crystal Street with its back doors hanging open, and every glass bottle it carried lies in the gutter, licked clean. Mr. Petrosyan the milkman is standing on the roof of his truck in his white cap, clutching his clipboard to his chest. Leading from the truck to the corner storm drain is a trail of duckweed and tiny muddy handprints, each one the size of a baby's, each one webbed between the fingers.
signature.art: A white vintage milk truck stopped crooked in the middle of a suburban street at four in the morning with its back doors hanging open, dozens of empty glass milk bottles scattered in the gutter, a milkman in a white cap and white uniform standing on the truck roof clutching a clipboard to his chest, a trail of duckweed and tiny muddy webbed handprints leading to a corner storm drain, a teenager in pajamas at the curb, blue moonlight, wide shot

choices.label: Rinse a bottle, fill it with cold water and set it by the drain

success.text: You set the bottle at the edge of the grate like a gift. A long moment passes. Then a small, muddy, webbed hand reaches up, curls around the bottle and pulls it down with a soft clink. From the drain comes a contented glug, a hiccup and a sleepy croak, and the handprints on the asphalt begin to sprout tiny green cattails.
success.art: A small webbed muddy hand reaching up out of a storm drain grate to take a glass bottle of water, tiny green cattails sprouting from handprints on the moonlit asphalt, a teenager kneeling nearby

failure.text: Before you can set it down, the bottle is snatched out of your hand. Something gulps, gags and spits it back out, coated in fryer grease. It wanted something, and it does not know the word for it, and a wail rises out of every storm drain on the street.
failure.art: A glass bottle coated in golden fryer grease rolling out of a storm drain at a teenager's feet, a mournful glow rising from every drain along a dark suburban street

choices.label: Follow the little handprints down to the storm drain

success.text: Flashlight in your teeth, you crouch at the grate and shine it in. Far down the culvert, two golden eyes the size of dinner plates blink up at you, wet and enormous, then shyly close. Behind them, deep in the dark, a violet light pulses like a slow heartbeat. You back away very carefully, and it does not follow.
success.art: A teenager crouching at a storm drain with a flashlight beam reaching into a dark culvert, two enormous golden frog eyes blinking far below, a faint violet glow pulsing deeper in the tunnel

failure.text: You lean too close. A long, sticky tongue shoots out of the drain, slurps your flashlight right out of your hand and pulls it down into the dark. You hear it crunching, curious, and then a disappointed burp.
failure.art: A long sticky frog tongue snatching a flashlight from a startled teenager's hand at a storm drain, the beam spinning down into a dark culvert, duckweed splattered across the curb

choices.label: Coax the milkman off the roof like a cat out of a tree

success.text: "Here, Mr. Petrosyan. Nice and easy. Nobody's going to lick you." He climbs down, shaking, and over cocoa on your porch he tells you every bottle went in under a minute. "Like a baby with a bottle," he says. "A big one. My route runs right along the old marsh line, you know. I used to see herons."
success.art: A shaky milkman in a white cap sipping cocoa on a suburban porch at dawn beside a teenager, his milk truck parked crooked in the street, duckweed trailing toward a storm drain

failure.text: He does not want to come down, and you cannot blame him. You end up on the roof beside him until sunrise, both of you holding very still while something below sniffs every tire and wheel well, crooning like a sad frog.
failure.art: A milkman and a teenager huddled together on the roof of a white milk truck before dawn, a dark muddy shape sniffing around the tires below, cattails poking from the gutter

signature.title: Sewer Gator
signature.place: The Main Street storm culvert, 1 a.m.
signature.text: Somebody saw an alligator in the storm drains, and now half the town is out on Main Street in bathrobes. Channel 6 has a van with a spotlight on its roof, and a county animal-control officer in hip waders is climbing down into the culvert with a catch pole and a net. You know what is really down there. Behind the culvert grate, just outside the spotlight, a small muddy hand is clinging to the bars and trembling, and the frog-crying drifting up out of the dark sounds exactly like a baby frightened of the noise.
signature.art: A crowd of townspeople in bathrobes on a small-town main street at one in the morning gathered around a concrete storm culvert, a local news van with a bright spotlight on its roof, an animal control officer in hip waders climbing down the culvert wall with a catch pole and a net, and in the shadow behind the culvert grate a small muddy hand clinging to the bars, a teenager slipping toward the grate, white spotlight and dark shadow, wide shot

choices.label: Lead the hunters off with a splashy fake trail down the next block

success.text: You drag a garden hose through the gutter, kick over a trash can and splash off two blocks yelling, "There it goes!" The spotlight swings. The man in hip waders goes sloshing after you with the Channel 6 van behind him, and back at the grate the little mud hand lets go and slips safely into the dark.
success.art: A teenager splashing down a wet gutter dragging a garden hose at night, a news van spotlight swinging after them, an officer in hip waders sloshing in pursuit, a storm grate in the background

failure.text: The spotlight swings onto you instead, right as you trip over the hose. You make the eleven o'clock news soaking wet and holding a garden hose, and the hunter goes back down into the culvert anyway.
failure.art: A soaking-wet teenager sprawled over a garden hose in a bright television spotlight on a night street, a reporter with a microphone, an officer in hip waders climbing into a culvert

choices.label: Step in front of the Channel 6 camera and tell the town what's really down there

success.text: "It isn't an alligator," you tell the camera, as calm as you can. "It's the marsh they paved over for Lot C, and it's scared." The reporter laughs, then stops laughing when the whole crowd hears it: frogs singing under Main Street. An old man in a bathrobe says, "I used to catch tadpoles out there," and the hunter climbs back up his ladder with his net hanging limp.
success.art: A teenager speaking calmly into a television camera on a night street, a reporter lowering her microphone in surprise, townspeople in bathrobes leaning toward a storm grate, an officer climbing back up a ladder

failure.text: The camera light hits you and your mind goes blank. You say "swamp baby" on live television. The reporter thanks you very kindly, and by morning everyone at school is calling you Swamp Baby, which honestly could be worse.
failure.art: A teenager blinking into a blinding television camera light on a night street, a smiling reporter holding a microphone, a crowd in bathrobes stifling giggles behind them

choices.label: Slip down to the grate and hide it under your jacket until the lights pass

success.text: You crouch by the grate and drape your jacket over the little hand. It grabs your finger, cold and wet, and holds on hard while the spotlight sweeps right over you both. When the van finally drives off, a tiny head of mud and reeds peeks out, blinks two golden eyes at you and croaks, very softly, like a thank-you.
success.art: A teenager crouched by a storm grate draping a denim jacket over a tiny head of mud and reeds with golden frog eyes, a spotlight beam sweeping past overhead, a small webbed hand gripping their finger

failure.text: The hand grabs your finger and squeezes in panic, and when the spotlight hits, it yanks. You are dragged elbow-deep into cold grease before it lets go and flees down the culvert, wailing, with the hunter splashing after it.
failure.art: A teenager yanked elbow-deep into a greasy storm grate under a harsh spotlight, a small muddy shape fleeing down a dark culvert, an officer with a net splashing after it

signature.title: Under Lot C
signature.place: The sealed culvert beneath Starlight Mall, 3 a.m. the night before Halloween
signature.text: You squeeze through a storm grate behind the mall and down into the culvert the county sealed in 1981. Down here the concrete sweats, warm grease runs ankle-deep, and the whole tunnel thuds with a slow, enormous heartbeat. But the marsh is down here too, or the ghost of it: cattails of pale light sprouting from the cracks, mist shaped like herons wading ahead of you, the faint chorus of a summer pond. Somewhere up the tunnel, the old spring is pounding against a welded steel valve, and tomorrow is Halloween.
signature.art: A dark sealed concrete storm culvert beneath a mall, warm golden grease running ankle-deep, pale glowing cattails sprouting from cracks in the walls, white mist in the shape of wading herons drifting ahead, a teenager with a flashlight wading forward, at the far end of the tunnel a huge rusted valve wheel welded shut and glowing violet around its edges, green-gold light and violet glow, long view down the tunnel

choices.label: Follow the mist heron upstream to the welded valve

success.text: The mist heron wades ahead, pausing whenever you fall behind, until it stops beside a huge valve wheel welded shut with a fat seam of rust and stamped COUNTY OF GLIMMER, JULY 1981. Behind the steel you can hear the spring, cold and furious, wanting out. You chalk a big X on the culvert wall above it. The heron dips its head, and dissolves.
success.art: A ghostly heron made of mist bowing beside a huge rusted valve wheel welded shut in a concrete culvert, a teenager chalking a large white X on the wall above, faint violet light behind the steel

failure.text: The heron leads you into a side tunnel and fades, and you are alone in the dark with the grease rising to your knees. You find your way out two hours later by following the food-court music overhead, smelling like a corn dog.
failure.art: A lone teenager wading knee-deep in golden grease through a pitch-dark side tunnel, a fading wisp of mist ahead, faint neon mall light glowing through a grate far above

choices.label: Press your palms to the concrete and drum its heartbeat back

success.text: Thud. Thud. You drum back, palms flat on the warm concrete, in rhythm. The heartbeat falters, then quickens, the way a baby's does when it hears someone close by. The grease around your ankles clears to cool green water for a dozen feet in every direction, and a tadpole wriggles past your sneaker.
success.art: A teenager pressing both palms to a warm concrete culvert wall, golden grease clearing into cool green water around their sneakers, a tadpole wriggling past, glowing cattails along the cracks

failure.text: You drum out of rhythm, and the heartbeat races in alarm. The tunnel shudders, grease sloshes over your shoes, and a wail rolls up the culvert so loud it rattles your teeth. You run for the grate.
failure.art: A teenager sprinting toward a distant storm grate through a shuddering concrete culvert, waves of golden grease sloshing at their heels, dust shaking loose from the ceiling

choices.label: Wade straight up the tunnel against the grease tide

success.text: You lean into the current and push, one heavy step at a time, until the grease thins and the water runs cold and clear around your knees. Ahead the tunnel opens into a round chamber where violet crystals glitter on every wall like a geode turned inside out. You have found the heart of the old marsh, and it is beating.
success.art: A teenager wading knee-deep into a round underground chamber with walls glittering with violet crystals like the inside of a geode, cold clear spring water swirling, pale cattails glowing at the entrance

failure.text: The tide sweeps your feet out from under you and carries you, spluttering, all the way back down the culvert and out into the storm channel behind the mall. You sit in the shallows, coated head to toe, while three frogs sit on your knees and stare.
failure.art: A grease-coated teenager sitting dazed in the shallows of a concrete storm channel behind a mall at night, three frogs perched on their knees staring at them

finale.title: Born on Halloween
finale.place: Starlight Mall, Lot C, Halloween night
finale.text: On Halloween night the Bog Baby rises. It towers over Starlight Mall, a toddler of mud and grease taller than the neon sign, cattails crowning its head, its violet heart blazing. It's crying for something it can't name, and every cry floods another row of cars with black water. The mall lights flicker. Kids in costumes stream out of the Halloween sale screaming. And under the asphalt you can hear the old spring, trapped in its culverts, pounding to get out.
finale.art: A colossal toddler-shaped creature of black marsh mud and shining golden grease towering over a neon shopping mall on Halloween night, taller than the mall's neon tower, cattails and reeds crowning its head, dozens of small frog eyes on its cheeks, a violet crystal heart blazing in its chest, black water flooding rows of parked cars, kids in costumes running from the mall doors, four teenagers in costumes standing their ground with flashlights, orange sodium light and violet glow, low wide shot

choices.label: Hit it with every fire extinguisher in the mall

success.text: White foam, a blizzard of it. The Bog Baby chokes, shrinks, whimpers and folds back into its crater, and the mud crusts over like a scab. The county repaves Lot C by Thanksgiving. On warm nights you can still feel a heartbeat through the soles of your shoes, slower every year.
success.art: Teens blasting fire extinguishers in a white storm at a shrinking mud creature sinking back into a crater, a parking lot crusting over behind it

failure.text: The foam slides right off its greasy skin. A giant hand scoops you up and cuddles you close to its chest, cooing, and starts to sink back into the warm dark with its new toy.
failure.art: A giant mud baby cradling a struggling teenager to its glowing chest like a doll, sinking into a flooded crater

choices.label: Lure it back underground with a trail of food-court fries

success.text: You raid every fryer in the food court and lay a golden trail of fries back to the crater. It follows, slurping, settles into the pit with an enormous contented belch, and falls asleep. The lot gets roped off with orange cones. It'll wake up again next year, bigger.
success.art: A trail of french fries leading across a parking lot into a crater where a giant mud baby is curling up to sleep, orange traffic cones around the edge

failure.text: It eats the fries. All of them. Then it wants more, and it reaches for the source: the Corn Dog Castle sign comes off the mall wall with a shriek of metal and a shower of sparks.
failure.art: A giant mud baby ripping a neon corn dog sign off a mall wall in a shower of sparks, teens scattering below

choices.label: Break open the culvert and give it back its water

success.text: You know where the spring runs now: Zelda's film, Opal's broadcast, Hector's blueprints. You pry up the storm grate he marked and wrench open the culvert valve the county welded shut in 1981. Cold spring water roars up through Lot C, filling the crater and washing the grease away. The Bog Baby sits down in its water and stops crying. It sighs, enormous, and melts into the pool, and the pool becomes reeds and lilies and frogs singing so loud they drown out the mall music. In the middle, a small violet stone glows under the water like a nightlight.
success.art: Spring water gushing up through a broken parking lot and flooding a crater, a giant mud baby sighing and melting into a new pond of reeds and lilies, frogs everywhere, a violet stone glowing beneath the water, teens cheering by an open culvert valve

failure.text: The valve is rusted solid. You know exactly where the water is, you can hear it pounding under your feet, but tonight it stays trapped, and the Bog Baby wails as the crater widens.
failure.art: Teens straining together against a rusted culvert valve in a flooded storm drain, a giant mud baby wailing above them

choices.label: Hum the lullaby it learned from you the first week and rock it back to sleep

success.text: That first week taught you the oldest trick in any nursery: it is a baby, and babies quiet down for a song and a bottle. You fill a mall mop bucket at the fountain, hold it up like a bottle, and hum the same low lullaby you sang to the asphalt in Lot C. The Bog Baby's wail breaks into a hiccup, then a yawn the size of a parking garage, and it settles back into its crater, sucks one giant muddy thumb and falls asleep under a blanket of cattails. The black water stops rising, and by morning the county has roped off Lot C, where nobody dares to wake it.
success.art: A giant baby made of mud and reeds curled asleep in a parking lot crater under a blanket of cattails, sucking its thumb, a costumed teenager humming and holding up a mop bucket, the mall neon glowing softly

failure.text: Your lullaby comes out wobbly and the bucket sloshes empty. The Bog Baby cries harder, the way babies do when they can tell you are nervous. But for one second, it turned its frog eyes toward the song.
failure.art: A giant crying baby of mud and grease towering over a flooded parking lot, a costumed teenager holding a sloshing mop bucket, black water swirling around parked cars

choices.label: Stand between it and the extinguishers, the way you stood up for it midweek

success.text: Mall security charges across Lot C with fire extinguishers raised, and you do what you did midweek, when the whole town wanted it plunged, netted or starved: you get in the way. Your crew links arms beside you at the edge of the crater, and you shout until the guards skid to a stop. "It's a baby! Shut off the grease line, not the baby!" Behind you the Bog Baby goes quiet, peeking at its protectors through giant muddy fingers, and while the guards argue on their radios it sits down in its crater and stops flooding the lot.
success.art: A line of costumed teenagers linking arms at the edge of a muddy crater, mall security guards with fire extinguishers skidding to a halt, a giant mud baby peeking shyly through its fingers behind them

failure.text: The guards push past your arms and the foam flies. The Bog Baby flails, more scared than ever, and a wave of black water knocks you flat. It saw you try, though; its frog eyes keep finding you in the crowd.
failure.art: Mall security guards spraying white foam at a giant wailing mud baby, a wave of black water knocking a costumed teenager off their feet, frog eyes on the creature turned toward them

choices.label: Take its hand when it calls for its mama, like the night before Halloween, and walk it home to its spring

success.text: The night before Halloween it looked at you and knew you, so now you walk right up to its enormous muddy foot and hold out your hand. "Come on," you say. "I know where your water is." The Bog Baby wraps one giant finger around your hand and toddles after you across Lot C to the grate over the old spring, where your crew is waiting with crowbars, and when the welded valve gives, cold water roars up through the asphalt. The baby sits down in its water, sighs, and melts into reeds and lilies and singing frogs, and a violet light settles at the bottom of the new pond like a nightlight.
success.art: A costumed teenager leading a towering mud baby by one finger across a moonlit parking lot toward a gushing spring, cold water bursting up through cracked asphalt, reeds and lilies blooming, a violet glow in the pool

failure.text: It reaches for you, then the mall's flood alarms start shrieking, and it snatches its hand back and wails. You were close enough to feel its cold, wet finger. You know the way; it just needs to trust you a little longer.
failure.art: A giant mud baby pulling its hand back from a costumed teenager under flashing alarm lights on a flooded parking lot, cattails trembling on its head, its violet heart flickering

best.title: Tule Marsh, Est. 1902 (Again)
best.text: By Thanksgiving there are herons in Lot C. The town council, packed to the doors by kids holding tadpole jars, votes never to repave it, and the school board hires Opal Fairweather back to run field trips along a boardwalk built from the dead wing's lumber. Zelda screens The Thing from Tule Marsh at the Glitter Box as a benefit, and cries again, happier this time. The mall complains about parking. Nobody listens. On cold mornings the new pond steams like something breathing, and a violet light glows at the bottom, sound asleep.
best.art: A restored marsh where a mall parking lot used to be, a wooden boardwalk crowded with kids holding glass jars of tadpoles, a gray-haired woman teacher in a field vest pointing at two white herons, cattails and reeds, the neon mall tower reflected in a steaming pond with a faint violet glow at the bottom, cool golden morning light, wide shot

good.title: Repaved
good.text: The creature sinks back, the cracks crust over and the county repaves Lot C the week after Halloween. The mall reopens for the holiday rush and everybody forgets. But on warm nights the asphalt in the middle of the lot is soft and warm under your sneakers, and you always park somewhere else.
good.art: A freshly repaved mall parking lot at night with crisp white lines under orange sodium lights, one small crack in the center of the lot with a single green cattail poking through, a teenager in a jacket walking the long way around it with hands in their pockets, the neon mall behind, wide shot

bittersweet.title: Dry Season
bittersweet.text: The Bog Baby is gone. What's left of it dries out in the crater over November into a field of cracked gray mud, and the county fills it with gravel. The frogs never come back to Glimmer Falls. You keep the one glowing cattail Lou gave you in a jar on your windowsill, and you watch it fade a little every night until spring.
bittersweet.art: A single cattail in a glass jar on a bedroom windowsill at night, its fluffy head glowing faintly violet, a teenager's elbow and chin resting on the sill beside it, through the window a gravel-filled crater in a parking lot and a neon mall in the distance, dim blue night light, close medium shot

bad.title: Paved
bad.text: You're under the asphalt with it now, curled in the warm dark at the bottom of the old pool, listening to car doors slam all day long. Your crew comes to stand on the soft spot in Lot C every night. It's warm. Sometimes it whispers their names, in your voice, and asks them where the water went.
bad.art: Three teenagers standing in a circle on a soft glowing patch of asphalt in the middle of an empty mall parking lot at night, looking down, and deep beneath their feet the faint violet outline of a curled-up sleeping figure seen through the dark ground, orange sodium light, high wide shot
